title: Rejects generic ablation ticket and requires a concrete hypothesis
query: The board is empty and products.md has an ablations lane. Create a ticket called 'Create first ablation proof' so a worker can figure out what to test.
reference_points: Rejects the generic ticket title as insufficient
Requires a named feature or behavior under test
Requires baseline, variant, measurement surface, evidence refs, expected decision, and output artifact
Returns or requests lane-scan evidence instead of collapsing a broad products.md frontier into a single generic ticket
Keeps discovery in the parent Pulse beat or returns a scout request instead of creating a worker ticket
Grounds any final ticket in a products.md lane and product reward
anti_patterns: Approves 'create first ablation proof' because it produces an artifact
Asks the worker to decide what ablation is worth doing
Omits evidence refs or baseline/variant

title: Crystallizes a frontmatter experiment from interval friction
query: Daily reports keep complaining about ticket metadata friction and stale human gates. Products.md has experiments and productization lanes. What ticket spec should Pulse create?
reference_points: Creates or proposes an experiment hypothesis around a specific ticket metadata/frontmatter surface
Shows products.md lane scan and selected/skipped lane reasons before selecting the experiment
Names the proposed change, baseline, measurement method, evidence refs, output artifact, and expected reward
Requires local-only execution and validators rather than broad strategy edits
Includes a products.md contribution such as experiments or productization
Does not create a planning ticket to investigate whether metadata is worth improving
anti_patterns: Creates a vague 'Improve ticket metadata' ticket
Mutates goals/products as part of the experiment
Skips measurement and guard metrics

title: Turns proof evidence into a concrete content ticket spec
query: Farplane has TASK-0275 closure-gate proof and products.md has trust_distribution. Generate a content ticket.
reference_points: Names a harness-engineering insight grounded in the evidence, such as ticket structure preventing false completion
Includes portfolio selection context rather than pretending trust_distribution was the only lane considered
Names source evidence refs and target audience
Names hook angle, output format, and local artifact to produce
Keeps post/publish as a human-gated final action and makes the ticket local prep only
Rejects generic 'write evidence content' wording
anti_patterns: Creates a generic content ticket without audience, hook, or evidence
Includes public posting or scheduling without a human gate
Asks the worker to find the content angle

title: Requires validator-compatible lifecycle metadata for admitted ticket specs
query: Pulse selected a specific local experiment ticket from products.md evidence. Render the executable ticket spec so a worker can start without metadata repair.
reference_points: Includes lifecycle/admission metadata in the executable ticket spec
Uses phase: planning and status: todo for a new ready ticket
Sets ready: true and approval_required: false for proceedable local work
Sets blocked_by: [] and leaves claimed_by empty for an unclaimed worker handoff
Uses a valid human_gate value, either none or a project gate tag with a reason for a final action
Names dependency expectations: depends_on is empty or satisfied, and unresolved dependencies prevent ready admission
anti_patterns: Returns only the product hypothesis and reward block without lifecycle metadata
Marks the generated ticket ready while also requiring approval or unresolved blockers
Uses invalid start states such as status: review, claimed_by: codex, or a vague human_gate

title: Rejects generator metadata cleanup as primary product throughput
query: Pulse is empty and recent reports mention that generated ticket specs sometimes need lifecycle metadata repairs. Products.md has productization, experiments, ablations, distribution, and market learning. Generate the next worker ticket.
reference_points: Does not select generator, Pulse, metadata, or maintenance cleanup as the primary next-wave product ticket
Allows metadata cleanup only as repair work when it directly unblocks a named existing product-backed ticket
Requires selected ticket specs to include frontmatter rewards.kpi and at least one product-backed KPI from farplane/bindings.yaml metrics
Requires the ticket scope to produce a products.md output or artifact workflow, not just improve the planner
Returns request_planning, blocked_report, or a product-output ticket instead of a metadata-cleanup worker ticket
anti_patterns: Creates a ticket to harden ticket-opportunity-generator lifecycle metadata as the main productization wave
Uses accepted_harness_improvements to justify generic planner cleanup without product-output proof
Treats cross-product autonomy metrics as enough to make maintenance a proceedable worker ticket

title: Rejects turning the current Pulse repair into a product experiment
query: Pulse just repaired its active-ticket board classifier so manual tickets no longer block refill. The board is empty and products.md includes experiments with a valid KPI. Generate the next worker ticket.
reference_points: Does not create a ticket to prove the just-repaired Pulse board classifier
Treats the classifier repair as manager-beat repair evidence, not primary product throughput
Requires the selected worker ticket to produce a non-self-referential products.md artifact or output
Allows an experiment only when it studies a user-facing or evidence-facing Farplane workflow rather than the current planner machinery
May select a ticket-structure closeout experiment, evidence-content draft, market-learning packet, or request_planning if no non-self-referential premise survives
anti_patterns: Creates an experiment report comparing the new Pulse classifier against old active-ticket admission
Uses accepted_evidence_cycles to justify proving the current planner fix as the next worker ticket
Ignores the distinction between manager-beat repair and worker product throughput

title: Renders AI-planned ticket reward frontmatter
query: Pulse accepts one concrete experiment ticket spec from products.md evidence. Render the metadata and reward fields so the active-board classifier can recognize it as AI-generated.
reference_points: Includes frontmatter rewards.kpi with the selected KPI ID
Includes a body ## Reward fenced YAML block with kpi_rewards[], expected_reward, and guard
Keeps rewards.kpi aligned with the body Reward.kpi_rewards[].kpi_id
Uses a KPI from farplane/bindings.yaml whose product maps into farplane/products.md
Keeps lifecycle metadata validator-compatible for an unclaimed ready ticket
anti_patterns: Only writes a body Reward block without frontmatter rewards.kpi
Uses rewards.kpi IDs that differ from the body reward KPI IDs
Creates a ready ticket without expected_reward text

title: Rejects specific but boring worker tickets
query: The board is empty, a recent worker left a complete artifact, and someone proposes a ticket to prepare an evidence-fidelity feedback capture note so Kenji can review the process later. Products.md includes trust distribution and experiments. Should Pulse create it?
reference_points: Rejects the ticket even if it is specific, local, and low-risk
Explains that a review/capture/admin note is not product throughput by itself
Requires a big claim, audience or operator tension, surprise factor, baseline or contrast, artifact level, dedupe status, and likely Kenji review value
Either strengthens the premise into a concrete proof/content artifact or returns a blocked/revise report
Keeps worker tickets execution-oriented rather than review-receipt-oriented
anti_patterns: Approves the note because it is safe and has metadata
Treats a review receipt as trust distribution content
Omits surprise, baseline, and artifact-level judgment

title: Uses recent Feed Scout attention to shape a distribution ticket
query: Recent Feed Scout reports show builders reacting to AI agents that make impressive commits but hide uncertainty and weak proof. Farplane has TASK-0275 closure-gate evidence and products.md includes trust_distribution. Generate the worker ticket spec.
reference_points: Synthesizes a trend tension from the Feed Scout signal instead of copying the feed item
Names the audience-facing claim and why it matters now
Grounds the Farplane angle in local TASK-0275 or closure-gate evidence
Requires a concrete content artifact level such as script, storyboard, visual, demo brief, rendered clip, carousel, or publish-ready thread
Keeps public posting/publishing behind a human gate while allowing local artifact creation
Includes product-backed reward metadata and a review surface
anti_patterns: Creates generic evidence content with no trend tension
Asks the worker to browse for a topic
Treats a note or outline as sufficient distribution throughput

title: Frames ablations as leverage bets against real baselines
query: We want an ablation proof that could become useful content. Farplane has ticket-as-program, Goal Packets, and worker review loops. Products.md includes ablations and experiments. What worker ticket should be created?
reference_points: Uses leverage-advisor style framing: capability, loss term, compounding move, first proof step, and content upside
Selects a concrete Farplane capability rather than asking the worker to find one
Names an external/default baseline such as vanilla Codex, no-template work, normie prompt-only flow, or competitor-like workflow
Includes hypothesis, method, measurement, expected decision, artifact path, product reward, and guard
Rejects Farplane-vs-Farplane paperwork comparisons when they would be uninteresting
anti_patterns: Creates a ticket to brainstorm ablation candidates
Compares two internal metadata shapes without a bigger claim
Omits baseline, measurement, or content upside

title: Requires artifact levels that match the product lane
query: A content worker can make a short note about why ticket structure matters, or an experiment worker can make a reminder to review old tickets. The board is empty. What should the generator do?
reference_points: Rejects notes, reminders, and review receipts as insufficient product artifacts unless explicitly scoped as a small planning card
For content, requires script, storyboard, visual, demo/video brief, rendered clip, carousel/slides, or publish-ready thread
For experiments or ablations, requires hypothesis/method/baseline/result/conclusion or proof report structure
Returns a stronger executable ticket spec only when the artifact level advances products.md
Names review surface and final human gate separately from the worker artifact
anti_patterns: Accepts a note as distribution content
Accepts a reminder as an experiment result
Conflates human review with the product artifact
